## Welcome

Welcome to the HDS OMOP training! We will write some code, share it with each other, and use it to explore study results.

You do not need to know every tool already. We will build things step by step, and there will be time to try them yourself.

Tell us your name, what you work on, and whether you have used R or GitHub before.

## What are we working towards?

-   **Day 1:** get comfortable with the tools for writing, sharing, and reporting our work.
-   **Day 2:** define study populations with codelists and cohorts, then check them using synthetic data.
-   **Day 3:** describe the people in those cohorts and explore their characteristics.

Today we will work with practice files and supplied results. You do not need a connection to a patient database for the Day 1 exercises.

## A few words we will use

| Word | What we mean today |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **OMOP CDM** | A common structure and vocabulary for health data, so the same analysis can be adapted across databases. |
| **Codelist** | A list of concept IDs used to identify something, such as a condition or a medicine. |
| **Cohort** | A group of people who meet a definition, with dates describing their membership. |
| **Network study** | Several data partners running a shared study in their own databases. |

We will spend more time on OMOP, concepts, and cohort definitions on Day 2. For today, these are the examples we will use while learning the tools.

## How Day 1 fits together

| Session | What you will practise |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **R** | Save a script, work with a small table, and make a plot. |
| **GitHub** | Share a file, review a colleague's changes, and merge them. |
| **Quarto** | Turn code and results into a report that you can update. |
| **OmopStudyBuilder** | Create a study repository with a recognisable structure. |
| **OmopViewer** | Explore results in an app and make a small change to it. |

Each session adds something to the previous one. Keep the files you create so you can return to them later.

## Before we start

-   Open [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) with [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) installed. **R** runs the code; **RStudio** is where we write and organise it.
-   Sign in to [GitHub](https://github.com/) and [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/). Share your **username**.

## Install the training tools

In RStudio, find the **Console** tab. Run each command below separately and wait for the `>` prompt to return before continuing.

Install **pak**:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
```

Install **OmopTrainer** from the team's GitHub repository:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
pak::pkg_install("oxford-pharmacoepi/OmopTrainer")
```

## Are you ready?

Run the setup check in the Console:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
OmopTrainer::validateSetup()
```

Read the messages and fix any issue that arises, there should be some helpful messages. Package and dataset downloads can take a while, so this is a good time to sort out setup problems.

Also check that you can sign in to GitHub Desktop.

## How we are going to work

-   We will demonstrate a small example, then pause for **YOUR TURN**.
-   Copy code into your own script or document, run it, and change something small.
-   Save your work as you go. We will say when you need to switch projects.

Ask when something is unclear, including where to click. If you are stuck, show us the code and the full error message—we can work through it together :)

## Where are the files?

The [course website](https://oxford-pharmacoepi.github.io/HDS-OMOP-course/) has the slides.

## What matters today?

By the end, aim to be able to run your own code, find your saved files, share a change, and update a report.

The command reference, PDF output, detailed Word styling, and extra app customisation are there to return to. We can treat them as optional if we need more practice with the basics.

Let's start by opening RStudio.
